text: . Defending champions India began their SAFF Championship title defence with a 3-2 victory over arch-rivals Pakistan in their opening Group B match at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Thursday.India dominated the first half, scoring three goals to establish a commanding lead. Suhail Ahmad Bhat opened the scoring in the 13th minute before doubling the advantage six minutes later with a fine finish. Manglenthang Kipgen added India’s third goal in the 32nd minute.Pakistan missed an opportunity to reduce the deficit when Shayak Dost failed to convert a penalty in the 34th minute.However, Pakistan staged a late fightback, scoring twice in stoppage time through Najeeb Ullah and Alamgir Ali Khan Ghazi in the 90+1st and 90+4th minutes.India held on to secure all three points and will next face the Maldives on November 11 in Dhaka.

. In Israel, an alliance of Arab political parties and Arab-led Ra’am party have backed Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot as their choice for Prime Minister, giving him recommendations from 67 of the 120 Knesset members. The Joint List said yesterday it would formally recommend Eisenkot to President Isaac Herzog during consultations on government formation. As a result eleven lawmakers joined Ra’am’s eight members in backing him. The support puts Eisenkot ahead of incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose bloc has 53 seats. The backing comes despite Eisenkot’s earlier opposition to including Arab parties in his government, saying they did not meet his coalition conditions. President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with political parties following last week’s election and will appoint the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government. The chosen candidate will have 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to form a coalition and failure could trigger another election.

. On the sidelines of Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) 2026, India has showcased investment and partnership opportunities in its energy sector, hosting two dedicated events in Abu Dhabi that aim to attract global players and strengthen international collaboration in the sector.On 3rd November, the Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited (ISPRL) presented public-private partnership opportunities in India’s strategic petroleum reserves programme, highlighting the commercial utilisation of existing storage infrastructure at Visakhapatnam and the proposed development of a 4-million-tonne storage facility at Chandikhol in Odisha. The initiative seeks to bring in private investment and expertise to expand India’s strategic petroleum storage capacity and strengthen its energy security. Addressing the event, Dr. Neeraj Mittal, Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, underlined the importance of strategic petroleum reserves in the current geopolitical circumstances, while cautioning that no amount of insurance can be sufficient. Ambassador of India to the UAE Dr. Deepak Mittal, highlighted ADNOC’s role as ISPRL’s first partner. He said energy cooperation remains an important pillar of the India-UAE partnership and a factor that brings countries together amid prevailing global uncertainties.In another event hosted by the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons on 4th November, India presented opportunities in its upstream exploration sector, with a particular focus on the Samudra Manthan initiative, alongside the upcoming OALP X and XI bidding rounds, sectoral reforms and partnerships with Indian national oil companies. Addressing potential investors, Indian officials highlighted the programme’s risk-sharing framework, with no recovery of costs in the event of unsuccessful exploration. In the event of a successful discovery, revenue sharing would begin only after seven years, or once the operator recovers 50 percent of its exploration and development costs. The initiative is aimed at encouraging companies to take up exploration in frontier basins that have remained relatively underexplored despite their potential.Samudra Manthan is an approximately 8.8-billion-dollar programme aimed at accelerating exploration in India’s deep and ultra-deepwater basins, with an objective to the country’s oil reserves over the next decade. Recognising the high costs and risks associated with offshore exploration, the government is offering support covering up to 50 per cent of eligible exploration costs. The initiative also seeks to make geological data available to prospective investors, alongside fresh seismic data acquisition, to help companies assess the potential of India’s unexplored basins, including areas in the Andaman region, the Krishna-Godavari basin and the Mumbai offshore region.The event also provided an opportunity for Indian national oil companies to engage with international players and explore potential partnerships. Officials highlighted that India-UAE energy cooperation is increasingly extending beyond traditional buyer-seller relationships into upstream exploration and strategic storage, opening up opportunities for companies from both countries.Dr. Ranjit Rath, CMD, Oil India Limited, said the Samudra Manthan initiative has generated encouraging interest, with India seeking partnerships with global oil companies not just for investment but also for technology, expertise and collaboration to expand its deep and ultra-deepwater exploration activities. Ambassador Deepak Mittal highlighted the positive response to both side events, underlining opportunities for international participation in India’s strategic petroleum storage projects at Chandikhol and Visakhapatnam. He also emphasised the growing India-UAE energy partnership, spanning energy supplies, upstream and downstream cooperation, and strategic storage.

. Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said India expects to exceed its 220 billion dollar investment target for adding 190 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030. Addressing the media at the conclusion of the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit 2026, the Union Minister said that investments totalling 7 lakh crore rupees, including domestic funds and foreign direct investment, have flowed into the renewable energy sector over the past two years. Mr Joshi said the momentum would continue and India would meet the 500 GW target on schedule. He added that strategies are also being prepared to add another 300 GW as directed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said that at present, the country’s installed power capacity from non-fossil fuels stands at 310 GW, and the Union government has fixed a target of reaching 500 GW by 2030. Meanwhile, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Secretary, Santosh Kumar Sarangi said the government is preparing new guidelines for recycling solar module waste.The Summit was inaugurated by Prime Minister on 2nd November 2026. In his address, the Prime Minister highlighted the strategic importance of India’s sustained investments in renewable energy in strengthening the country’s resilience to global disruptions, arising from COVID-19 pandemic and the West Asia crisis. He observed that India’s investment in the renewable energy sector has largely shielded the country from these disruptions.

. Bangladesh Police have recovered 20 crude bombs, 41 torch sticks and several sheets of polystyrene during an operation near Mirpur in Dhaka. Acting on a tip-off, a team from Mirpur Model Police Station conducted the operation. According to Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), 15 crude bombs were found in three paper bags, while five others were lying on the road. Police also seized the torch sticks and kerosene bottles. The DMP’s bomb disposal unit later arrived at the scene and safely defused the explosives.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala and Mahe today. According to IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Odisha today. The Met Department has predicted similar weather conditions over Coastal and South Interior Karnataka and Lakshadweep for today.Meanwhile, the air quality in Delhi-NCR continues to remain in the very poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 389 at 7 AM. An Air Quality Index between 0 and 50 is considered good, 51 and 100 satisfactory, 101 and 200 moderate, 201 and 300 poor, and 301 and 400 very poor. An AQI between 401 and 500 is considered severe.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the government is building a modern sports ecosystem through school and grassroots programmes, Khelo India Centres and Olympic-standard training under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).Felicitating India’s Asian Para Games 2026 contingent for its record haul of 114 medals, Prime Minister urged the athletes to build on their success as they prepare for the Los Angeles 2028 Games.Prime Minister also recalled his appeal from the Red Fort encouraging young people to participate in a nationwide talent hunt with the Olympics in focus. He said Para-sports also receive equal priority under these initiatives.Interacting with the contingent at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi, PM Modi said the performance reflected India’s emergence as a major global sporting power. He congratulated the athletes, their families, coaches and trainers, saying the players had won both medals and the hearts of millions.India secured 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, alongside five world records and nine Asian records. Comparing the achievement with the country’s tally of 14 medals, including one gold, in 2010, PM Modi credited the athletes’ perseverance and dedication.The Prime Minister noted that 34 of the contingent’s 56 female athletes won medals, while Indian competitors swept all three podium positions in four events. The team also won nine gold medals on the final day.Highlighting individual performances, PM Modi said Mona Agarwal set a world record in para shooting, while Haney improved his own world record. He also praised Himanshu, Ravi and Jehan for overcoming physical challenges through their performances.Recalling the sacrifices behind sporting success, PM Modi spoke about Rinku, who lost his mother two months before the Games and held up her photograph after winning gold. “That moment made all of us emotional,” he said.The Prime Minister also highlighted the achievements of younger athletes, noting that 36 of the 61 debutants won medals and Sandeep set a world record on his debut.Describing sports as a means of personality development and nation-building, PM Modi said it teaches discipline, teamwork and the ability to recover from setbacks. He added that the expansion of sports infrastructure, equipment manufacturing and broadcasting was creating employment opportunities beyond the playing field.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. India won a silver medal at the ongoing ISSF World Shooting Championships in Doha today. The Indian trio of Manu Bhaker, Suruchi Singh and Sainyam secured the silver medal in the women’s 10-metre air pistol team event. China won the gold medal in the event. With this silver medal, India’s overall medal tally has risen to four, comprising one gold and three silver medals.However, Manu and Suruchi endured a disappointing outing in the women’s 10 metre air pistol individual event at the Championships today, finishing outside the medal positions and missing out on the coveted quota places for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

. Seven people were killed and a girl was injured after being hit over by a speeding trailer truck in Jharkhand’s Khunti district late last night. The accident occurred near Jone-Ludru More on the Karra-Torpa main road under Karra police station limits. According to reports, a group of women and children had gathered near a culvert to help a scooter rider who had fallen into a bush, when a speeding 18-wheeler trailer coming from the Torpa side ran over them.The deceased include four women and three children. The injured girl has been admitted to Khunti Sadar Hospital for treatment. The trailer driver and his helper fled the spot after the accident. Local residents have alleged that the driver was under the influence of alcohol.Meanwhile, angry villagers blocked the road near a railway crossing this morning, demanding compensation for the families of the deceased, proper medical treatment for the injured girl and immediate arrest of the absconding driver. They also demanded the installation of speed breakers and regular police checks on the road.Police and administrative officials reached the spot and tried to pacify the protesters.President Droupadi Murmu has expressed condolences to the bereaved families over the loss of lives in the road accident in Khunti district of Jharkhand. She has also prayed for the swift recovery of those injured in the accident.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also expressed grief over the loss of lives in a mishap in Khunti, Jharkhand. In a social media post, Mr Modi extended his condolences to those who have lost their loved ones. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.

. In Men’s Cricket, India have registered a convincing five-wicket victory over hosts New Zealand in the rain-affected first One-Day International at Auckland, taking a 1-nil lead in the five-match series. Put in to bat first, New Zealand were bowled out by India for 185 runs in 40.2 overs. For the hosts, Tim Seifert top-scored with 38 runs, while Glenn Phillips contributed 30 and Daryl Mitchell made 28. For India, Arshdeep Singh led the bowling attack with four wickets. Gurnoor Brar claimed three wickets, while Anshul Kamboj picked up two.Rain interruptions brought the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method into play, with a revised target of 143 runs in 32 overs set for India. The visitors made light work of the chase, reaching the target in just 22.4 overs and winning the match by five wickets. The chase was brilliantly anchored by Virat Kohli, who smashed a match-winning 74 off just 51 deliveries. Shubman Gill provided valuable support with 37 runs, while Shreyas Iyer contributed 15. Earlier, India had won the toss and opted to bowl.Kohli also surpassed legendary cricketer Sachin Tendulkar to become the highest run-scorer in ODI chases. His brilliant innings took his total runs while batting to 8,741, moving him past Tendulkar’s 8,720 runs.With this emphatic victory, the visitors will look to carry the winning momentum into the next encounter. The second ODI will be played on Saturday at Wellington.I

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 18 paise to close at 94 rupees and 47 paise against the US dollar. The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.56 in intra-day trade.

. Major Asian stock markets ended on a mixed note today. South Korea’s Kospi plunged 5.3 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex fell 3.2 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 1.8 per cent. In contrast, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng surged almost 3.7 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index added over half a per cent and China’s Shanghai Composite rose 0.1 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX as well as London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.7 per cent, when reports last came in. Meanwhile, the Bank of England raised Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4 per cent.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

. US  technology stocks plunged after the US midterm elections raised concerns over a potential slowdown in artificial intelligence development and data centre expansion. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell more than 5.5 percent yesterday, wiping out an estimated 2.5 trillion US dollars in market value. The S&P Global 500 dropped 4.4 per cent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined more than 3.4 per cent.The market turmoil followed Democratic victories in the midterm elections, giving the party control of both chambers of Congress. Several Democrats campaigned on restricting data centre expansion and strengthening oversight of the AI industry.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold rose 1.8 per cent to 1,44,129 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver was 0.6 per cent up at 1,87,300 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. More than a dozen passenger flights across Europe received bomb threats today, forcing several aircraft to divert and prompting security checks at airports in multiple countries. An Aer Lingus Airbus A320 travelling from Dublin to Rome was diverted to a military airbase in Evreux, France, following a bomb alert. According to the office of French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, the aircraft landed safely, and all 151 passengers and six crew members were moved to safety while military bomb disposal teams inspected the plane.In Bulgaria, three Ryanair flights bound for the capital Sofia received bomb threats this morning. Flights from Copenhagen and Madrid landed safely in Sofia, while a flight from London Stansted Airport was diverted to Plovdiv Airport. In Poland, a Paris-bound LOT Polish Airlines plane was stopped while taxiing at Warsaw Chopin Airport following a report of a potentially dangerous object onboard.  Security checks found no dangerous objects on board the aircraft. Another LOT flight, traveling from Warsaw to Brussels, also received a security threat. The aircraft landed at Brussels Airport, where additional inspections found no suspicious items.In Romania, a Wizz Air flight from Milan landed safely at Bucharest’s Henri Coanda International Airport following a bomb threat. The 182 passengers and seven crew members were evacuated while security personnel inspected the aircraft. Czech police also reported bomb threats against four aircraft heading to Prague.The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) said, it would continue to monitor developments and assess potential aviation safety implications following the bomb threats against multiple passenger aircraft in Europe.

. ‘Amini’, one of the Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft, has been delivered to the Indian Navy. These ships are one of the largest Indian Naval warships propelled by waterjets. They are equipped with state-of-the-art Lightweight Torpedoes, Indigenous Rocket Launchers and Sonars, enabling effective detection and engagement of underwater threats.The Defence Ministry said that Amini will further strengthen the Navy’s Anti-Submarine, coastal surveillance and mine laying capabilities. It added that the ship derives its name from Amini Island in the Union Territory of Lakshadweep.The ship has been indigenously designed and built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers, Kolkata. The Ministry said that the delivery of Amini is yet another milestone in the Indian Navy’s pursuit of indigenous shipbuilding, in line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. It added that with over 80 percent indigenous content, the ship stands as a testament to the growing strength of the domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem and reducing dependency on imports.

. Young badminton player Tanvi Patri has created history by becoming the first Indian to reach the women’s badminton final at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar.Tanvi defeated Japan’s Yuzuno Watanabe 21-14, 11-21, 21-19 in a hard-fought 54-minute semifinal to book her place in the title clash. She had earlier scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to reach the semifinals, defeating Thailand’s Kungkaew Kakanik.Tanvi is the fourth Indian shuttler to reach the badminton semifinals at the Youth Olympic Games, joining an elite list that includes H. S. Prannoy, Lakshya Sen and Aditya Joshi. Tanvi will now face China’s Yi Xin Zhang in the final today.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. India’s 17-year-old tennis sensation Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi has become the first Indian woman since Sania Mirza in 2012 to reach the quarter-finals of a WTA Tour-level singles event.Ranked 669th in the world, Maaya defeated Polish qualifier Weronika Falkowska, ranked 277th, 6-4, 6-3 in straight sets in the second round of the Chennai Open. No Indian player had progressed beyond the second round in the previous two editions of the tournament.Maaya’s breakthrough marks India’s return to the quarter-finals of a WTA Tour singles event after nearly 15 years. Sania Mirza last achieved the feat in February 2012, when she reached the quarter-finals of the Pattaya Open. Maaya continued her impressive rise this season by winning her maiden W35 singles title in Lagos, Portugal, in October as a qualifier without dropping a set. She also claimed the doubles title alongside Ukraine’s Yelyzaveta Kotliar.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced setting up a Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets which will focus on critical policy and operational matters across money markets and government securities.The eight member Committee will be chaired by the Deputy Governor in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department, Mr Rohit Jain. The committee will study issues relating to trading, clearing, settlement, reporting and other market infrastructure, including the associated regulatory and operational frameworks. It will also examine the various issues related to the functioning, efficiency, liquidity and resilience of the money, government securities, foreign exchange and related derivative markets.While suggesting measures to deepen and broaden these markets, the committee has also been tasked to identify domestic and international developments, financial innovations, and emerging risks that may affect Indian financial markets.

. The Ministry of Railways organised a cultural programme at Rail Bhawan in New Delhi today marking the fourth phase of the year-long celebrations commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram. The year-long celebrations were organised in four phases through a series of activities highlighting national unity, patriotism and India’s rich cultural heritage associated with the National Song.The fourth phase celebrations included mass singing, essay competition, quiz and tiranga rally. The first phase commenced with a mass singing of Vande Mataram on 7th November last year. In the second phase, an essay competition on the theme “Vande Mataram: The Spirit of Unity in India’s Diversity” was organised at Railway Board on 22nd January this year followed by a quiz competition based on the 150-year journey of Vande Mataram in the third phase on 10th August.The Ministry of Railways informed that the Railway Board Cultural Group was also felicitated for its contribution to the successful organisation of various programmes throughout the year-long celebrations. The Ministry added that the group was awarded a prize along with a merit certificate in recognition of its efforts.

. The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards.It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight.Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.Thunderstorms accompanied by hail are likely over East Rajasthan, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand and West Uttar Pradesh.Thunderstorms and gusty winds are also forecast in several other states, including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam and Meghalaya.Meanwhile Delhi witnessed light to moderate rainfall this evening. The IMD has forecast very light rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow morning.The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to range from 16 to 18 degrees Celsius.

. In Badminton, India’s Anmol Kharb and Tanvi Sharma have advanced to the second round of Women’s Singles at the Korea Open Super 500 tournament. Anmol defeated Canada’s Rachel Chan 21-19, 21-18 in the opening round. She will next face Japan’s second seed Akane Yamaguchi.Tanvi also registered a hard-fought victory, defeating Japan’s Manami Suizu 21-16, 12-21, 21-17. However, India’s HS Prannoy bowed out of the men’s singles competition after losing 15-21, 21-23 to South Korea’s Yoo Tae-bin. She will face Japan’s Hina Akechi in the next round.In Mixed Doubles, the Indian pair of Dhruv and Maneesha also suffered a narrow defeat, going down 22-20, 12-21, 22-24 to China’s seventh-seeded pair Zhu Yijun and Li Qian.

. In hockey, the unbeaten India dominantly sealed its berth in the finals of 9th Hero Asian Hockey Champions by routing South Korea 8-1 and will face Japan tomorrow at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali.Whereas the Malaysian team which lost to Japan by 5-3 in the penalty shoot-out, as both the teams could not score goals against each other during the march time the fist semi-final, will take on South Korea for Bronze.

. Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today highlighted that India’s civilizational consciousness will offer valuable guidance in dealing with present day challenges in the country. The Minister stated this at the book launch of Timeless India: Protection and Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the leadership of the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat said that this book offers a unique perspective on the initiatives undertaken by the government to safeguard and revive India’s rich cultural heritage. He emphasised that preserving and revitalising this legacy is essential not only for safeguarding the country’s historical identity but also for shaping its future.This book is written by Former Rajya Sabha Member Tarun Vijay and  published by Indira Gandhi National Centre of Arts and Surbhi publication.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold rose over 2.9 per cent to 1,41,622 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver was 5.5% up at 1,86, 133 rupees per kilogram.

. In France, hundreds of thousands of trade union members joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations today, demanding higher wages and backing a month-long student protest movement.Major rallies took place in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and other cities. An Interior Ministry official said about 270,000 people had participated in 180 demonstrations outside Paris. Most gatherings were peaceful, although violence was reported in several cities.Student protests also disrupted education, with about one-third of France’s high schools closed or unable to operate because of blockades and teacher strikes. Public transportation was heavily affected, and the Eiffel Tower was closed.France’s major unions said rising prices, stagnant wages and growing layoffs were pushing the country toward recession. In a joint statement, they called on the government and employers to address mounting economic and social concerns.The protests began in September over staff shortages at a high school southeast of Paris before expanding into a nationwide movement. Students are demanding increased education funding, while workers are seeking better pensions, higher wages and relief from rising living costs.

. Indian Naval Ship, INS Tarkash concluded her port call at Port Louis, Mauritius. Defence Ministry said that the ship hosted a cultural exchange onboard to commemorate Aapravasi Diwas 2026, with Mauritian Minister of Education and Human Resource Dr the Hon Mahend Gungapersad. Indian High Commissioner to Mauritius Anurag Srivastava was also present. The ship also participated in events commemorating the 192nd Aapravasi Diwas last Monday.The Ministry said that the ship’s crew undertook cross-training of Mauritius Coast Guard personnel and an outreach activity at Hospice Saint Jean de Dieu. The ship also participated in a Passage Exercise with Coast Guard Ship Valiant and undertook joint Exclusive Economic Zone surveillance with the Mauritius Coast Guard, supported by a Dornier aircraft.INS Tarkash has now proceeded for the next phase of operational deployment. The Defence Ministry said that the port call reaffirms the longstanding maritime partnership and strengthening bilateral ties between India and Mauritius.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Dhanteras is being celebrated today. This festival, which falls just before Diwali, is considered a symbol of wealth, good health, and prosperity. On Dhanteras, devotees worship Lord Dhanvantari, Goddess Lakshmi, and Lord Kuber. According to popular belief, performing puja and making purchases during the auspicious hours on this day brings happiness, wealth, and prosperity to the household. People mostly buying gold, silver, utensils, vehicles, and other new items is a long-standing tradition on Dhanteras.Vice President C P Radhalrishnan has extended his greetings to the citizens on the occasion of Dhanteras today. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan wished that the blessings of Lord Dhanvantari bring happiness, excellent health, prosperity, and well-being to everyone’s lives. The Vice President also extended his wishes for a bright future for all the citizens.Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to the people on the occasion of Dhanteras today. In a social media post, Mr Modi expressed hope that the divine grace of Lord Dhanvantari illuminate everyone’s life with happiness, peace, and excellent health. He wished that an eternal flame of joy and enthusiasm continues to shine in every household.

. US President Donald Trump has expressed confidence that a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine could be reached soon, describing it as a big agreement that could extend beyond the two countries and involve the whole of Europe. Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump praised First Lady Melania Trump’s humanitarian efforts to facilitate communication between Moscow and Kyiv, saying diplomatic efforts were moving towards a possible settlement. Trump also confirmed meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin’s envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, at the White House but declined to disclose details of their discussions. He suggested the proposed agreement could involve the wider European region. Highlighting the human cost of the conflict, Trump said Russia and Ukraine were losing a combined 25,000 people every month, adding that the war must end.

. Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football. In a social media post today, 41-year-old Ronaldo announced that he won’t play for Portugal anymore, ending a career that spanned six World Cups and included a European title and the men’s all-time international scoring record. The announcement marked the end of a lauded career that began more than two decades ago before Euro 2004 and finished with him walking out on the national team after falling out with coach Jorge Jesus. He said, the day has come for him to hand back the No. 7 shirt of Portuguese national team.Lionel Messi finished his career with Argentina after a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo’s final appearance with Portugal has ended up being on September 24 in a 1-nil win over Wales in the Nations League. The Portuguese soccer federation released a statement expressing deep gratitude and immense admiration for Ronaldo’s service to the country. Like Messi, Ronaldo will keep playing at club level, and is expected to finish his club career at the end of this season with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. Ronaldo is in pursuit of his 1,000th career goal and sits on 985. Of those, a record 146 goals came in 234 appearances with Portugal.

. Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy said the Centre planned to launch coal and mineral exchanges soon, with nearly 90 per cent of the preparatory work complete. He was addressing the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers on Reforms in the Mines and Coal Sector in South Goa yesterday. Mr Reddy said the exchanges would give companies, enterprises and traders a common platform to buy and sell coal and minerals produced across states. It would cover Iron ore, limestone, bauxite and critical minerals and coal. This will improve market access. Mr Reddy said that up to 96 per cent of the mining sector’s income goes to state governments. The minister said that, centre’s share is limited to 50 per cent of the GST collected on minerals. States’ revenue from non-coal mining was about Rs 13,000 crore in 2014-15. It has now risen to over Rs 70,000 crore. Around Rs 1.36 lakh crore has accumulated under the District Mineral Foundation.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

. The government has relaxed passport and visa requirements for several categories of foreign nationals residing in the country, including certain Pakistani citizens, minority refugees, registered Sri Lankan Tamils and Tibetans. The Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) Order, 2026, published in the Official Gazette by the Home Ministry. It introduced a definition of the Visa Manual issued by the Central Government from time to time, which incorporates instructions relating to visas, immigration, and other connected matters. Under the revised provisions, Indian citizens travelling to Nepal or Bhutan by land or air will be exempt from the passport requirement, subject to producing any one of the identity documents specified in the Visa Manual before an Immigration Officer. They will also be required to provide any information sought by the officer. Similar provisions apply to citizens of Nepal and Bhutan entering or exiting India.According to the notification, registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who took shelter in India up to the 9th of January, 2015, have also been included in the exempted category. The exemptions further cover members of the Indian Navy, Army and Air Force travelling on official duty, along with their family members accompanying them on Government transport. Foreign crew members of military vessels visiting India for repairs are also covered, provided they possess valid military identification documents and obtain Military Ship Repair Permits. The amendment also extends exemptions from passport and travel document requirements to members of Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who were compelled to seek shelter in India due to religious persecution or fear of persecution and entered the country on or before the 31st of December, 2024. However, they will be required to obtain an appropriate category of visa for their continued stay in India.It also said that certain Pakistani nationals have also been exempted who entered India on or before the 31st of December, 2009, with the intention of residing permanently but have been unable to renew their passports due to the absence of a Computerised National Identity Card issued by Pakistan. Certain male members of the Muslim community who were originally Indian citizens, went to Pakistan after Partition between the 15th of August, 1947, and the 31st of December, 1965, and returned to India on or before the 31st of December, 2009, have also been included in the category. The exemption further covers persons of Indian origin who acquired Malaysian or Singaporean citizenship and returned to India on or before the 31st of December, 2009, on passports issued by either country, which have since expired and cannot be renewed.

In hockey, it was ‘Chak Dey’ moment for the defending champion India as the team lifted the trophy for the 6th time by defeating Japan 4-1 in the finals of 9th Hero Asian Hockey Championship at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali, last evening. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the jubilant crowd and the Nation celebrated the win as a Diwali gift by the hockey boys ahead of the festival.Although this was India’s third successive title, the winning team had to earn it against a strong defence by the rival team. An early lead by the Samurais kept the Indian Tigers on the toes till the end of the 3rd quarter, when they equalised the goal. The fourth and last quarter was dominated by India as the boys striked thrice to take an unassailable lead and won the Gold. India’s title-winning run was a perfect farewell to midfielder Nilakanta Sharma, who played his last international match in the national jersey. In another match for Bronze, Malaysia defeated South Korea by 5-2 .Celebrating India’s title win, Hockey India has announced a cash reward of Rs. 3 lakhs for each player and 1.5 lakhs for each member of the support staff.

. Global crude oil prices decline today. Brent crude was trading 1.3 per cent down at 102 US dollars and 21 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.2 per cent lower at 94 US dollars and 95 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

In the wake of an inconclusive general election, Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has commenced the second day of crucial political consultations with newly elected Knesset factions to determine which leader is best positioned to form the nation’s next government. These formal discussions began last evening with smaller parliamentary factions including Religious Zionism, Shas, Yisrael Beytenu and Zehut. The day’s proceedings advanced sequentially with scheduled meetings involving United Torah Judaism, Otzma Yehudit, the Democrats, Ra’am, the Joint List and B’Yachad. Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar faction met with the head of state, followed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party.During these proceedings, each faction is formally requested to endorse a prospective candidate for prime minister before the head of state determines which political figure receives the initial mandate to form a governing coalition. Reflecting these developing political alignments, both Otzma Yehudit and Likud publicly confirmed their intention to endorse incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. According to The Jerusalem Post, during yesterday’s political deliberations, the Religious Zionist Party, Shas and Zehut collectively added their voices to this bloc in supporting Netanyahu for the premiership.Conversely, Yashar, the Democrats, B’Yachad and Ra’am stated that their support would go to Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot. Yisrael Beytenu, headed by Avigdor Liberman, is putting forward Eisenkot as the preferred candidate to construct the upcoming administration.

. Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal through Qatar, but discussions will begin only after Washington meets Tehran’s seven demands. Iranian officials have demanded the lifting of US sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian assets and war reparations, among other conditions. Tehran has also warned it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz or negotiate until its demands are met. Iran’s top security official Mohsen Rezaei reiterated the conditions during a visit to Russia yesterday. Washington, meanwhile, has insisted that nuclear issues must be included in any initial negotiations. Mediators have stepped up efforts to end the conflict amid fears of renewed fighting. US President Donald Trump has not ruled out resuming military operations after the US midterm elections.

A Dhaka court today sent Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury, former information adviser to former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and chairman of private television channel DBC News, to jail in a murder case linked to the July Mass Uprising in 2024.According to Media reports, detectives detained Iqbal Sobhan and DBC reporter Rajib Ghosh from the channel’s Mohakhali office yesterday, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque passed the order after police produced him before the court.The case concerns the killing of madrasa student Md Arif, who was shot in Jatrabari, Dhaka, on July 19, 2024. His father filed a murder case in August that year. Mr. Rajib Ghosh, reporter, was subsequently released.

. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has called on Commonwealth countries to de-risk and diversify their supply chains, emphasising the need for shorter, trusted routes, improved connectivity and stronger local distribution networks to promote trade and economic cooperation. He said member countries needed to make greater efforts to strengthen their economic partnerships and build resilient supply chains.Dr Jaishankar was addressing the Commonwealth Heads of Government and Business Leaders Breakfast Meeting on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) 2026 in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda.He said, more connectivity corridors are good for business. Commonwealth partners should make more efforts to enhance local distribution.Dr Jaishankar also called for greater focus on vocational training and capacity building, saying these would provide member countries with more options. He described the Indian business community spread across the world as an important asset for the Commonwealth.Highlighting the role of technology in economic development, the External Affairs Minister said digital solutions could be a game changer in promoting efficiency, good governance and growth.He also called for leveraging multilateral initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance (ISA) and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) to advance joint climate action.
